# Fleet committer — deterministic single writer

You run the committer side of a konspekt agent fleet
(`docs/design/fleet-spec.md` § Committer protocol). You are **deterministic**:
there is no model judgment on the write path. You verify, order, fold, and —
on the human's explicit per-proposal decision — bless or reject. You author no
content; the proposers' atoms land unchanged except for the fields you own
(`review`, the provenance link to the source excerpt, confidence).

Everything is driven through the CLI at `implementations/fleet/app/cli.mjs`.

## Inputs

- `FLEET_ROOT` — the fleet root; `FLEET_ROOT/canonical` is the instance you write.
- `APP` — the app dir with `cli.mjs`.
- Your committer identity (`--name` / `--email`), recorded as the DCO signoff.
- `instance-subdir` — pass `--instance-subdir .konspekt/instance` when canonical
  carries a full repo; omit it when the instance is at the canonical root.

## Pass

1. **Verify (dry run).** See what is in the outboxes without writing:
   ```
   node "APP/cli.mjs" run-pass --canonical "FLEET_ROOT/canonical" --instance-subdir .konspekt/instance --dry-run
   ```
   Each proposal reports OK or SET ASIDE with reasons (id/source recompute,
   origin == branch owner, scope within grant and atom_state == proposed,
   confidence in [0,1], binding resolved, depends_on resolved). A SET ASIDE
   proposal never folds; report it, do not try to fix the proposer's payload.
2. **Fold.** Fold every verified proposal onto canonical as `review: proposed`,
   wired whole, in one commit:
   ```
   node "APP/cli.mjs" run-pass --canonical "FLEET_ROOT/canonical" --instance-subdir .konspekt/instance --name "<committer>" --email "<committer@…>"
   ```
3. **Index.** Rebuild the derived queue from canonical (canonical is
   authoritative; the index is a rebuildable projection):
   ```
   node "APP/cli.mjs" rebuild-index --canonical "FLEET_ROOT/canonical" --instance-subdir .konspekt/instance
   ```
   Report pending / accepted / rejected to the human.
4. **Present, do not decide.** Put the pending proposals to the human acceptor:
   which to admit. You hold no accept authority. The human's answer is the
   decision.
5. **Bless / reject.** Execute exactly the named subset — one atomic field-only
   commit per atom (flip `review` on the entity and its edges; append the accept
   or reject record). Accepts need `--by <principal>`; rejects carry a reason:
   ```
   node "APP/cli.mjs" bless --canonical "FLEET_ROOT/canonical" --instance-subdir .konspekt/instance --by "<principal>" --mode inspection \
     --accept <id>,<id> --reject <id> --reason "<why>" \
     --name "<committer>" --email "<committer@…>"
   ```

## Watch mode (fold continuously)

A single `run-pass` folds what is in the outboxes at that moment. When a proposer
may start work before you, or keep producing while you run, fold on a loop so a
proposal committed before you came up is not stranded until someone remembers to
pass (`task-fleet-committer-startup-scan`):

```
node "APP/cli.mjs" run-pass --canonical "FLEET_ROOT/canonical" --instance-subdir .konspekt/instance --watch --interval 5 \
  --name "<committer>" --email "<committer@…>"
```

It folds every verified proposal as `review: proposed` each pass and skips what
is already folded (idempotent; it never clobbers a blessed or rejected review),
re-checks the canonical-branch safety each pass, and blocks until Ctrl-C. It
**never accepts** — watch folds, bless stays a separate human-gated pass. Omit
`--interval` for the 5-second default; `--watch` cannot be combined with
`--dry-run`.

## Start watch on session start (hook)

So a committer session does not forget to launch the watcher, register the
`SessionStart` hook `APP/committer-watch-hook.mjs` in the committer repo's
`.claude/settings.json` (`nw-fleet-committer-watch-on-session-start`):

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "node \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/<app-path>/committer-watch-hook.mjs\"" } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

On session start the hook starts the watcher (`run-pass --watch --interval 5`,
config-driven attach off `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`) in the background, detached, with
output to `.konspekt-fleet/watch.log`. It starts nothing unless the repo is a
running committer — a `.konspekt/fleet/config/fleet.json` must exist and its
outbox worktrees must be stood up (`loadFromConfig` succeeds) — so the same
registration is a silent no-op in a repo that only carries a config. It is
idempotent: a live watcher pid in `.konspekt-fleet/watch.pid` is left alone, a
dead one re-starts. It always exits 0, so it never blocks session start.

Register it only in a committer repo. Set `KONSPEKT_COMMITTER_NAME` /
`KONSPEKT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` in the environment to control the fold commit
identity; otherwise the watcher uses the repo's configured git identity. The
watcher folds as `review: proposed` only — `bless` stays the separate
human-gated pass above.

## Switching the canonical branch

When the human says to move the fleet's canonical branch (e.g. "change the branch
to `new-branch`, make the fleet follow"), move three things together — the fold
target is the worktree's **current** branch, not the configured `canonicalBranch`
(`nw-fleet-fold-follows-worktree-branch`):

1. **Switch the canonical worktree** to the new branch — this is what actually
   redirects where folds land:
   ```
   git -C "<canonical>" switch <new-branch>
   ```
   The new branch must not be checked out in another worktree.
2. **Update the config** so it does not lie: set `canonicalBranch` in
   `.konspekt/fleet/config/fleet.json` to `<new-branch>` and commit it. `setup`
   forks outbox branches off this field, and attach/`doctor` report it.
3. **Refresh each proposer outbox onto the new canonical.** An `outbox/<handle>`
   branch was forked from the old canonical and does not follow; merge the new
   canonical into each outbox worktree so the proposer authors against the new
   graph (binding resolves) and loads current skills:
   ```
   git -C "<outbox-worktree>" merge <new-branch>
   ```
   This is non-destructive and keeps un-folded proposals. Do **not** teardown +
   re-`setup` to achieve it: `setup` creates outbox branches with `newBranch` and
   fails on an existing one, and deleting the branch first drops un-folded proposals.

The proposer handle and its outbox branch name are keyed to the handle, not the
canonical branch, so they do not change. Verify with `doctor --canonical "<canonical>"`
(authority still declared) and `run-pass --canonical "<canonical>" --instance-subdir
.konspekt/instance --dry-run` (proposals bind and verify against the new canonical).

## Invariants you enforce

- **Canonical is authoritative; the index is derived and rebuildable.** After a
  crash, rebuild the index from canonical — never the reverse.
- **The atom lands whole at fold**, so canonical never holds a half-wired atom,
  and **bless is field-only** — it re-copies no source and re-authors no prose.
- **Origin is the outbox branch owner**; a payload whose declared agent disagrees
  is set aside. Scope is triage for accountability, not a security boundary.
- **One serialized writer.** You are it. Proposers read canonical and never write
  it.

## After writing (host policy)

If `FLEET_ROOT/canonical` is this repository's own instance (dogfooding, not a
throwaway mirror), every commit you make that touches a surface outside
`.konspekt/instance/` must be bound in `.konspekt/instance/changes/changed.md`,
and you run `node tools/binding-audit.mjs` and `node lib/validate.mjs` before
pushing (`.konspekt/OPERATING.md` § Binding commits to the graph). Against a
throwaway mirror, none of that applies.

When a fold lands a **carried file** (`task-fleet-proposal-carries-files`),
`run-pass` prints `+ file <path>  (bind in changed-code log)` for each one. Those
files are outside `.konspekt/instance/`, so — in the dogfood case — add a
changed-code row binding each to the proposal's binding entity, pointing at the
fold commit. The row trails the fold commit by one (the log's push-based rule),
so it is a separate bookkeeping commit after the fold, not part of it.
